title: all most some any no/none
subtitle: most people / most of the people
summary: Use all/most/some/any/no + noun for people and things in general, and all of/most of/some of/none of before the, this, my, them and it.

lesson.heading: In general or a special group?

left.label: children / money / books
left.text: No *the*. We are talking about people or things in general.

right.label: the children / the money / these books
right.text: We are talking about one special group.
examples: I want to buy a car, but I haven't got **the money**.
I often go out with **my friends**.

lesson.heading: most / some + noun (no of)
lesson.text: Use **all**, **most**, **some**, **any** and **no** with a noun and *no* **of** when you talk about things in general.

examples.text: He's got **no friends**. I don't want **any money**.

lesson.heading: most of / some of + the/this/my ...
lesson.text: Use **of** before **the**, **this**, **that**, **these**, **those**, **my**, **your** and other words like these. Note that after **of** we say **none**, not *no*.

examples.text: **Most of the children** at this school are under 11 years old.
I don't want **any of this money**.
**Some of these books** are very old.
**None of my friends** live near me.

lesson.heading: The two patterns
rows: all / most / some / any / no + noun
**All the students** passed. or **All of the students** passed.
all / most / some / any / none + **of** + it/them/us/you
'How many of these books have you read?' '**None of them**.'

lesson.heading: all the ... or all of the ...
lesson.text: With **all** you can use **of** or leave it out. Both are correct.

examples.text: **All the students** in our class passed the exam. *or* **All of the students** ...
Silvia has lived in London **all her life**. *or* ... **all of her life**.

lesson.heading: all of it / most of them / none of us

examples.text: You can have **some of this cake**, but not **all of it**.
*A:* Do you know those people? *B:* **Most of them**, but not **all of them**.
**Some of us** are going out tonight. Why don't you come with us?
I've got a lot of books, but I haven't read **any of them**.

lesson.text: Use **no** with a noun (*He's got no friends*), but **none of** before the/my/them (*None of my friends live near me*).

exercises.explanation: children in general, so most + noun with no of.
people in general, so some people (not some of people).

exercises.prompt: ___ the shops in the city centre close at 6.30.
exercises.explanation: Before the we need of: most of the shops.
Before this we need of: some of this money.

exercises.prompt: You can change your money in ___ banks.
exercises.explanation: banks in general, so most banks with no of.
Before my we say none of, not no of.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the right answer.

pairs.left: Nine of the ten people are women. How many of the people are women?
The five boxes are all on the table. How many of the boxes are on the table?
Two of the six men are wearing hats. How many of the men are wearing hats?
Every window in the building is closed. How many of the windows are open?
The money on the table is all Sally's. How much of the money is Ben's?

exercises.prompt: I don't like ___ the pictures in the living room.
exercises.explanation: Before the we need of: any of the pictures.

exercises.prompt: The weather was bad when we were on holiday. It rained ___ the time.
exercises.explanation: Before the we need of: most of the time.

exercises.statement: Some of people work too hard.
exercises.explanation: Some people work too hard. We do not use of before a noun in general.

exercises.statement: I haven't seen any of those people before.
exercises.explanation: Correct: before those we use of.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order to describe a primary school.
exercises.answer: Most of the children at this school are under 11 years old.
exercises.explanation: Before the we need of: most of the children.
